The buggy method is `org.jfree.chart.util.ShapeList.equals(java.lang.Object)`.

Evidence:
- [`ShapeList.equals()`](org.jfree.chart.util.ShapeList.equals(java.lang.Object)) just delegates to `AbstractObjectList.equals()`.
- [`AbstractObjectList.equals()`](org.jfree.chart.util.AbstractObjectList.equals(java.lang.Object)) compares entries with `ObjectUtilities.equal(get(i), other.get(i))`.
- [`ObjectUtilities.equal()`](org.jfree.chart.util.ObjectUtilities.equal(java.lang.Object, java.lang.Object)) ultimately calls `o1.equals(o2)`.

That is incorrect for `ShapeList`, because many `Shape` implementations are not value-equal via `equals()`. In the failing test, both lists contain distinct `Line2D.Double` instances with the same coordinates; those objects compare unequal by identity-based `equals()`. The same problem reappears after serialization, where deserialization creates new shape instances.

So the root cause is not in serialization logic itself; it is that `ShapeList.equals()` relies on generic object equality instead of shape-specific geometric equality.
